case: Caldera Market: investor choice and equilibrium
provenance: Original synthetic one-period teaching economy, created 2026-10-08. No actual security, investor, market forecast or empirical observation.
units: Prices/payoffs/wealth in CU; shares in units; returns and variance in decimal simple-total-return units; risk aversion applies to return variance.
assumptions: All investors have common physical beliefs, maximize the stated mean-variance objective, trade divisible risky claims with unrestricted short sales, and borrow or lend at the same risk-free rate. Cash claims have zero aggregate net supply. No taxes, fees, interim distributions, outside labor income, other wealth or funding constraints exist. A separate explicit borrowing-limit experiment changes only investor 1's feasible set.
sample_scope: Eight selected pedagogical observations, each an allowed draw from the same four-state distribution; zero-based indices. They are not market data, a probability estimate, an exhaustive sample, a simulation result or a performance backtest.

mean_shift_experiment.scope: Increase every state return by the same amount while holding prices, supplies, wealth and risk aversion fixed. Recompute demands; report nonclearing rather than calling this a new equilibrium.

limits: The lab evaluates candidate prices and specified mean-variance demands; it is not a price-discovery algorithm or empirical inference engine. Candidate pricing weights are valid only if their positivity and every claim-price identity pass. General state-price theory follows in c05. Named selectors are used dynamically; alternative feasible inputs can return market_clearing=false.
